questions.stem: Why were ancient towns almost always built beside rivers?
questions.explanation: A river gave drink, fish and a way to move goods. With no roads, water was the easiest road there was.

questions.stem: Why did people invent writing in the first place?
questions.explanation: The first tablets are lists of grain and cattle. Literature came a long time after bookkeeping.

questions.stem: Why did the printing press change so much?
questions.explanation: A manuscript took months to copy; a press made hundreds. Ideas travelled faster than rumour for the first time.

questions.stem: What did Magna Carta actually establish?
questions.explanation: It bound the king to rules, mostly for barons. The idea that power has limits outlived every clause in it.

questions.stem: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin with cloth?
questions.explanation: Everyone needs clothes, so the market was already waiting. A machine paid for itself fastest there.

questions.stem: What happened to towns during the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: Factories called for workers and the countryside moved in. Housing and clean water did not keep up.
Colonies supplied cheap raw materials and bought finished goods. The flag usually followed the ledger.

questions.stem: Why did a Second World War follow the First?
options: There were simply not enough weapons
The peace was built as punishment
questions.explanation: Harsh terms and a broken economy grew resentment, and new regimes rose on it.

questions.stem: Why do historians compare several accounts of one event?
options: One source may be wrong or lying
To find the oldest one of them
questions.explanation: Every witness has an interest and a faulty memory. Independent accounts agreeing is the only real proof.

questions.stem: What does the word revolution mean in history?
options: A sharp break in the order
questions.explanation: A revolution changes how power and property work, not merely who holds them — and usually fast.

questions.stem: Why did the abolition of slavery not end inequality?
questions.explanation: Freedom arrived without land, capital or schooling. The law moved in a day; the arrangement of wealth did not.

questions.stem: Why do winners and losers write different histories?
options: One of the sides studied badly
questions.explanation: Choosing which facts to tell is already interpretation. One event can honestly be a triumph and a tragedy.

questions.stem: Why is the printing of newspapers important to democracy?
options: They employ a great many writers
questions.explanation: People can only decide together if they argue from the same information. That is why press freedom is fought over.

questions.stem: Why is it risky to judge the past by today's standards?
options: There were no written laws then
questions.explanation: People decide inside their own time and knowledge. Understanding a decision is not excusing it, but without that history becomes a courtroom.
